surprise.title: The internet's first word was "lo"
surprise.body: At 10:30 PM Pacific on October 29, 1969, UCLA student programmer Charley Kline tried to log in to a computer at the Stanford Research Institute over the brand-new ARPANET. He got two letters through, "l" and "o," before the Stanford machine crashed. About an hour later, after SRI programmer Bill Duvall adjusted it, the full login worked, and that was the first host-to-host connection on the network that grew into the internet. Telnet and FTP, the remote login and file transfer protocols you meet in A+ networking, were among the first things built on top of it. Same date, 1998: John Glenn flew on Space Shuttle Discovery at age 77, the oldest person ever to reach Earth orbit. Three days to sailing.
